title: ID0449225-DC/Si-D/TR-[Y2 / R4 313059181006]-Billing Issue Due to Incomplete Charging Session
description:
Reported behavior/issue:
User starts a charging session, but it doesn’t initiate due to an improperly connected plug, and a subsequent user inadvertently continues the incomplete session, causing incorrect billing.
Root cause: NA
Solution: After rebooting,
On DAMEX Sanctioned List: No
Warranty Status:
Active
One of our CPOs came to us with a complaint. They think it's related to the software. The issue is this: A vehicle starts charging from the app, gets to the final step, but then, probably because the socket isn't fully plugged in, unplugs the socket and leaves the station. Immediately after, another user takes over this unfinished process for their own vehicle and continues the charge that someone else started.
Naturally, when the person who couldn't start the charge receives the bill, they say, “This charge isn't mine.” Could such a situation occur? The case they forwarded to me is 101302214.  ELYA CENTER DC-2

additional_info.subject: RE: 0449225 - ID0449225-DC/Si-D/TR-[Y2 / R4 313059181006]-Billing Issue Due to Incomplete Charging Session CRM:00472000393
additional_info.body:
Hello Cardoso,
Fırst of all, thanks for your  detailed review,
In this case, it appears that when the customer initiated the charging session, the connector was not properly secured during the cable check phase, and therefore, the charging did not commence. Meanwhile, another driver at the same station connected their vehicle to the same connector and successfully started charging.
Due to the system logic, the billing was applied to the user who initiated the first session via the app, even though their vehicle was not charged. That is why the customer claims, “I started the charging but my car was not charged, and still I received the invoice.”
Although there is no technical fault on the system or charger side, this situation can create confusion from the user perspective.
As a potential improvement, additional guidance to ensure correct connection, or enhancements in the billing process to avoid such cases, could be considered.
That's why I don't think it's right to tell the customer it's a user-related error. If you want to review another case, I can send you another one.
Thanks for your supooırt.
